note: Rewritten to the claim that survived the four independent audits. Each statement below is the strongest version no auditor refuted; the original is kept on the entry so the correction is visible rather than silent.

problems.original_statement: Agreement between an emulation and a randomized trial raises confidence, and disagreement can arise from emulation failure, random error, different adherence, different measurement, different populations, or a limitation of the trial itself. RCT-DUPLICATE and the 2026 concordance meta-analysis both show better agreement under closer emulation and neither shows equivalence: across 107 paired emulations and trials the effect correlation was 0.59 overall and 0.83 among the 63 pairs judged to emulate more closely. What no one has is a theory that licenses the inference from those results to a new question: how much confidence a successful replication of trial A in database D transfers to question B in database D, or to question A in database E. Publishing after the trial result is known also creates design-calibration and selective-reporting risks that the concordance statistic cannot see.
problems.correction_note: The claim that no theory exists was too strong in one direction and too weak in another. Frameworks for transferring benchmarking confidence have been proposed and are unevaluated for that role, so the honest statement is that transfer is model-dependent rather than unattempted. The entry also treated prospective blinded benchmarking as an untried proposal; it has been done at least once.
problems.statement: A successful replication calibrates one emulation of one trial in one database. Transferring that confidence to a different question, or to the same question in a different database, is not an inference the benchmarking design licenses: it requires a target performance estimand stated in advance, an explicit selection or transport model, conditional exchangeability across the questions being compared, and overlap in whatever modifies emulation quality. Outside that support the transfer is model-dependent rather than identified, and frameworks that have been proposed for it remain unevaluated in that role. The benchmarking corpus is also a selected sample: trials get emulated when they are recent, large and have an accessible active comparator, which are the conditions under which emulation works best. Across 107 paired emulations and trials the effect correlation was 0.59 overall and 0.83 among the 63 pairs judged to emulate more closely, which measures performance on that favorable subpopulation and not on the questions a decision maker actually brings.
problems.why_open: The benchmarking set is not a random sample of questions, and no design would make it one: a trial has to exist before it can be emulated, and the trials that exist are not the questions for which trials do not. Attributing a discrepancy requires knowing which of six candidate causes produced it, and the data that would separate them, particularly the trial's own adherence and measurement, are usually unavailable to the emulator. Publishing after the trial result is known also creates design-calibration and selective-reporting risks that a concordance statistic cannot see, and only a prospective design removes them.
problems.proposed_direction: Extend prospective, blinded benchmarking, in which the emulation protocol and code are frozen and registered before the trial reports, from the isolated instances that now exist to a standing suite. Model concordance hierarchically by data source, clinical setting, outcome type and degree of protocol match, so what is estimated is a conditional expectation of agreement rather than a global rate, and state the target performance estimand before the comparison rather than after. Treat benchmarking as calibration evidence about a data source and a design class, never as certification of a method.

problems.original_statement: Agreement between an emulation and a trial is informative only when the estimands, populations and measurements are close enough to be comparable, and better design alignment is empirically associated with stronger concordance. Benchmarking nonetheless reports success or failure as a binary label, usually derived from whether the confidence intervals overlap or whether the direction agrees. That label mixes estimand mismatch with random error: two studies estimating the same quantity with wide intervals will agree by that criterion, and two estimating different quantities precisely will disagree. The reported statistic therefore does not measure what its users take it to measure.
problems.correction_note: The entry attributed the binary label to the benchmarking programs. They do not use one: RCT-DUPLICATE reports several agreement metrics and the 2026 concordance meta-analysis reports correlation and standardized agreement related to design features. The reduction to pass or fail happens downstream, in how those results are cited, which is a different and narrower claim.
problems.statement: Agreement between an emulation and a trial is informative only when the estimands, populations and measurements are close enough to be comparable, and better design alignment is empirically associated with stronger concordance. The benchmarking programs report this in graded form. What is cited downstream is a binary label, usually derived from interval overlap or direction agreement, and that label discards magnitude and uncertainty and cannot diagnose why two estimates differ: two studies estimating the same quantity imprecisely agree by that criterion, and two estimating different quantities precisely disagree. No reported measure, graded or binary, separates estimand mismatch from random error, because doing so requires aligning the estimands first and then reporting a paired contrast with joint uncertainty, which no benchmarking report currently does as a matter of course.
problems.why_open: Separating estimand mismatch from random error requires a distributional claim about the trial's own error that trials do not publish, so the criterion that would do it cannot be computed from what is available. Aligning estimands before comparison is possible and expensive, and it reduces the number of comparable pairs, which is the resource benchmarking is short of. The binary label is also convenient for the audiences who cite benchmarking results, so the pressure to replace it runs the wrong way.
problems.proposed_direction: Align estimands before comparing, then report the paired contrast with joint uncertainty, heterogeneity and any prespecified tolerance that a categorical judgment would rest on, so a pass or fail is derived rather than assumed. Report ratio of effects, absolute effect difference, standardized agreement and prediction-interval coverage together, so estimand mismatch and random error remain separately visible. Prefer prospective forecasts of a trial's result to retrospective comparison, and replicate across databases as well as across questions, since a data source's calibration is what a decision maker needs.
